sections.title: 1. Formation of the Constituent Assembly
sections.content:
The Constituent Assembly of India was formed to draft the Constitution of India. It was established as a result of the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946, proposed by the British government to transfer power to Indians.

Total strength: 389 members (296 from British India, 93 from Princely States, and 4 from Chief Commissioners' provinces).

sections.title: 2. Committees of the Constituent Assembly
sections.content:
The Constituent Assembly formed several committees to study various aspects of constitutional provisions. The most prominent committees included:

  • Drafting Committee: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar (Chairman) — prepared the draft Constitution.
  • Union Powers Committee: Jawaharlal Nehru — dealt with Centre-State relations.
  • Provincial Constitution Committee: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel — framed provincial constitutions.
  • Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights: Sardar Patel — dealt with Fundamental Rights and Minorities.
  • Steering Committee: Dr. Rajendra Prasad — managed the day-to-day affairs.
